producer_report.summary:
I revised docs/design/decision-sets.md to record the failed first `athena backtest` and the design changes it forced. I also added a matching addendum to review 1 and a CHANGELOG entry. Nothing was built or run; only the three doc files changed, and the boundary-word scan of the design files found nothing.

What the design now says:
- **Backtest section (new §9):** The run failed. The supersession parse had 24 hits and none lacked a target. One hit was unexpected: D11 at line 322, "Revised ... superseded by D39". The D87 signal (class docs, threshold 2) found 0 jobs.
- **Partial revisions:** These are `amended_by`, not `superseded`, because `superseded` drops the whole decision from briefs and would lose the part that still governs. D11/D39 is added to the expected list.
- **D87 signal:** The real interventions are class code. Job 20261013-192156-ar1x (9h2j) is the hand squash of PR #41 after the HTTP 405, and the only one after D87 was recorded. kn3q and qk2d predate it. D87's signal is revised to class code.
- **Hard and soft signals:** A host error that falsifies a stated assumption puts the decision under review on its first occurrence. Soft signals such as friction need repeats.
- **Host-error record:** The design says the `athena.host-error/1` record (review F3) is needed so the 405 is no longer only in intervention prose. It is placed first in the build order.
- **Signal validation:** Signal values are checked against the record vocabulary when written and when loaded, so a signal cannot name a class nobody records. This addresses the root cause of the D87 miss.
- **Common-sense signal:** A rule that rejects work not going against its stated intent is a failure signal for that rule. It cites the BRIEF.md addendum "2026-10-14: Common sense over rigid rules".

I could not read records/, so the backtest figures and ids come from your request and are marked as reported in the doc.
